project.title: DP-PFN: Differentially Private Prior-Data Fitted Networks
project.domain: differential privacy / prior-data fitted networks / machine learning

question.text: How can prior-data fitted networks (TabPFN, NodePFN) be used for differentially private tabular and graph prediction so that weights cost no privacy budget, while certificates come from black-box wrappers or noise-aware post-processing rather than from training loss?

hypotheses.text: If PFN weights are trained only on synthetic prior data and preprocessing is shard-local or public, privacy accounting reduces to the context release. A black-box Vote/LogPool/Student wrapper, or a noise-aware reader of an already-private summary S=M(D), is (ε,δ)-DP regardless of approximation error (Prop. 0, Cor. B4, Thm. D1).

No bound on PFN training loss certifies worst-case DP (Prop. B2). On closed-form floored priors, the log-gap Λ(D) and row-sensitivity s(θ,n) stay small on prior-typical datasets but can be driven large on adversarial neighbouring pairs; a more accurate PFN leaks more unless the training target itself is private (Obs. B5).

At fixed ε, DP-PFN-Vote sample size n* is set by teacher error e(m) at small shard size m (Thm. C2). A PFN teacher therefore attains a smaller n* than per-shard trained PATE teachers, and the minimizing m matches the C2 prediction.
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 4; tested by E2, E3

hypotheses.text: A PFN trained with the release mechanism inside the prior matches the private-data posterior predictive. Versus naive TabPFN on the same release, it reduces under-confidence on label randomized response and over-confidence on bulk DP synthetic rows, lowering NLL and ECE at the same ε (Thm. D1, Prop. D2).
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 5; tested by E4, Gate 2

history.text: Proposal read end-to-end (25 pages). Hypotheses H1–H4 registered from Sections 1–5. No experiment has been run; E1–E8 remain planned. Background citations in the PDF were not re-checked by the authors.
